description_full: ADT Inc. provides security, interactive, and smart home solutions in the United States. The company offers burglar and life safety alarms, smart security cameras, smart home automation systems, and video surveillance systems to detect intrusion; control access; sense movement, smoke, fire, carbon monoxide, leaks, temperature, and other environmental conditions and hazards; and address personal medical emergencies, such as injuries or unanticipated falls. It also provides routine maintenance and installation services for upgraded or additional equipment; and personal emergency response system products and services to sustain independent living, detect when a fall occurs, and provide protection while on the go with geolocation capability. In addition, the company offers ADT+ app, an interactive technology platform; Trusted Neighbor, which allows customers to grant access to their homes through homeowner-authorized credentials and the ADT+ app; automation and smart home solutions, which allow for the remote monitoring and managing of spaces through smartphone applications, customized web portals, and touchscreen panels; and professionally installed and DIY security and smart home solutions. Further, it operates monitoring centers that provide professional and outsourced monitoring services; and field and call centers. The company sells its products under the ADT, ADT Pulse, and ADT+ brands. It serves the residential and small business security and automation markets comprising owners and renters of single-family homes, apartments, and small businesses owners through customer referrals, door-to-door activities, lead generation partners, retail and e-commerce channels, network of field sales and service offices, third-party independent dealers, and authorized dealers. The company was formerly known as Prime Security Services Parent, Inc. and changed its name to ADT Inc. in September 2017. ADT Inc. was founded in 1874 and is headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida.

financial_summary: ADT Inc. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $7.2B market cap on $5.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +2.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $1.7B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.8× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 19% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 33% over the last three months.

With annualised volatility of 44% and a beta of 0.94, it moves roughly with the market.

val: The stock trades 83% below its DCF fair value of $56.99, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 49%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $43.34 to $76.99 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 13.0 vs 24.1, EV/EBITDA 5.5 vs 13.4 and P/FCF 4.2 vs 22.9 (sector median).

Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 23.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 8.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $10.00 on average, 1% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 7.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.93).
It converts 33% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 3.16x.
ROE of 16% is amplified by 4.2x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.8x net debt to EBITDA ($80.8M of cash against $7.7B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, and interest cover is thin at 2.8x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.70 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.93 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -7.1% over 3 years and -0.7% over 5 years, so the decline is deepening, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.2% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.04 and a backlog worth 72% of annual revenue.
Capex runs only 0.1x depreciation (3.4% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.

Insiders have only bought over the past year (5 purchases, net $477K bought).
It returns 11.0% a year to shareholders (8.4% in buybacks and 2.2% in dividends).
